questions.stem: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “Nowadays more and more people keep learning new skills to adapt to a fast-changing world.” You can make comments, cite examples, or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
Nowadays more and more people keep learning new skills to adapt to a fast-changing world. This trend, in my view, is not a passing fashion but a wise and even necessary response to the age we live in.

The most obvious reason lies in the speed of technological change. Skills that guaranteed a stable job ten years ago may become outdated overnight, so those who stop learning risk being replaced. Take my cousin as an example. As a traditional accountant, she felt threatened when her company introduced financial software, yet instead of complaining she spent her evenings mastering data analysis. Within a year she was promoted rather than laid off. Her experience convinces me that continuous learning is what keeps a person competitive. Beyond the workplace, learning also enriches our daily life and broadens our horizons.

In conclusion, keeping pace with a changing world through lifelong learning is no longer optional but essential. Rather than fearing change, we should treat every new skill as a bridge to a wider future. I firmly believe that whoever embraces new skills today will stand firm tomorrow.

sections.note: 本场次听力只有一份音频，本套听力与同场第一套同卷；原文、题目与答案取自该套真题。考场多套卷的选项顺序可能不同，这里沿用第一套的顺序。在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: W: Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure. Today, we go on a different kind of adventure: Jackson's life of parenting his offspring. David, as a parent of an 11- and a 14-year-old, what is the most interesting issue you are dealing with right now?
transcript.zh: W: 大卫·杰克逊先生是《纽约客》的一名专职撰稿人，以创作冒险类非虚构作品而闻名。今天，我们要进行一次不同类型的冒险：杰克逊养育子女的生活。大卫，作为一个有一名11岁和一名14岁孩子的家长，你目前正在面对的最有趣的问题是什么？

transcript.text: M: It's easy to focus on the challenges, but so far, I find these ages to be kind of wonderful. They are independent, and they have their own curiosities and obsessions. You can talk to them about fairly sophisticated subject matter such as politics.
transcript.zh: M: 人们很容易把注意力集中在挑战上，但到目前为止，我觉得这个年龄段还是相当美好的。他们很独立，也有自己的好奇心和痴迷点。你可以和他们谈论政治之类相当复杂的话题。

transcript.text: W: Yes, that does sound refreshing compared with talking to younger children. Do they ask you to proofread their essays?
transcript.zh: W: 是的，和年幼的孩子交谈相比，这听起来确实令人耳目一新。他们会让你帮忙校对作文吗？

transcript.text: M: Certainly, with writing they do. I really just try to be encouraging. I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement.
transcript.zh: M: 会的，写作方面他们确实会。我真的只是尽量给予鼓励。我认为，在这个年龄段，编辑方面的指导不如鼓励重要。

transcript.text: W: Are there books that you think are important that your children read, and that all children read?
transcript.zh: W: 有没有一些你认为很重要、应该让你的孩子读，也应该让所有孩子读的书？

transcript.text: M: My general thought is to read widely and to incorporate a love for reading. Learning to love to read, I think, is the optimal thing, because it gives you a skill you can take anywhere.
transcript.zh: M: 我的总体想法是广泛阅读，并培养对阅读的热爱。我认为，学会热爱阅读是最理想的事情，因为这会赋予你一种可以带到任何地方的技能。

transcript.text: W: So you're not too concerned like some parents with the content they're reading? I know I have some worries about that.
transcript.zh: W: 所以，你不像一些家长那样太在意他们阅读的内容？我知道自己对此有些担忧。

transcript.text: M: Yeah, read what you like. If a child loves graphic novels or comic books, whatever it is, that is turning them on to read and turning on their imagination.
transcript.zh: M: 是的，喜欢读什么就读什么。如果孩子喜欢图像小说或漫画书，不管是什么，只要能让他们喜欢上阅读，激发他们的想象力就好。

transcript.text: W: I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence. I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager. What do you think?
transcript.zh: W: 我觉得，随着孩子步入青春期，他们对书籍的品味会发生变化。我知道自己十几岁时确实发生过这种变化。你怎么看？

transcript.text: M: I think it's especially important as they get older to read subject matter that'll open their eyes to the world and people. So I think both fiction and non-fiction are really important because they give you the power to begin to perceive the world through the lives of others.
transcript.zh: M: 我认为，随着他们年龄增长，阅读一些能让他们开阔眼界、了解世界和他人的内容尤其重要。所以我觉得，小说和非虚构作品都非常重要，因为它们赋予你一种力量，让你开始通过他人的人生来感知这个世界。

questions.stem: What do we learn about David Jackson from the conversation?

options.text: He is an author of fiction.
He is a father of four kids.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure.信号：开场介绍句直接报身份 。主持人开场第一句就用同位语把人物头衔报全：a staff writer at the New Yorker。人物介绍题的答案信号就是这种"姓名 + 同位语头衔"的引入句，听到立刻锁定。

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：原文说他 is known for his non-fiction books of adventure——写冒险题材的书，是"写冒险的人"不是"亲历冒险的人"。He is an adventurer. 盗用 adventure 一词，把"写冒险书"偷换成"他本人是冒险家"，听到 adventure 就选会中招。 借用原文：non-fiction books of adventure
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：原文明确是 non-fiction books（纪实/非虚构），He is an author of fiction. 却说他写 fiction（虚构小说），正好把 non-fiction 的 non 抹掉、极性反了。听到 fiction 这半个原词就选，等于没听清前面的否定前缀。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：原文只说他有 an 11- and a 14-year-old（一个 11 岁、一个 14 岁，共两个孩子），He is a father of four kids. 凭空说"四个孩子"。four 这个数字原文从未出现，是偷改数字的陷阱。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a staff writer at the New Yorker ↔ He is a staff writer. 原句同位语→选项主系表，几乎原词对应）

questions.evidenceText: Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure.

questions.stem: What does the man think of young teenagers?

options.text: They are interested in fairy tales.
They are a headache to their parents.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P2）：They are independent, and they have their own curiosities and obsessions.信号：被问者的正面评价应答 。女方问他这阶段孩子的情况，男方应答先说 I find these ages to be kind of wonderful，再具体说 They are independent, and the…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：原文说能和孩子聊 sophisticated subject matter such as politics，即谈"成熟话题如政治"，反衬他们不幼稚；They are interested in fairy tales. 童话与原文要表达的"能聊成熟话题"恰恰相反，且 fairy tales 原文根本没提，是借"孩子"语境硬造的话题。 借用原文：I find these ages to be kind of wonderful
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：男方明明说 I find these ages to be kind of wonderful（觉得这年纪很好），They are a headache to their parents. 却说孩子让父母头疼，与他的正面评价完全相反。这是把褒义答案反向设成贬义的陷阱。 借用原文：such as politics
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：原文说能和孩子聊 politics，恰恰说明他们"懂/能聊政治"；They are ignorant of politics. 盗用 politics 原词，却说他们"对政治无知"，意思正好反过来。听到 politics 就选会直接掉坑。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（They are independent ↔ They are curious and autonomous. independent=autonomous 同义替换）

questions.evidenceText: They are independent, and they have their own curiosities and obsessions.

questions.stem: How does the man help his kids with their essays?

options.text: He offers them ample editorial guidance.
He recommends model essays to them.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：I really just try to be encouraging. I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement.信号：取舍句 less important than 落在后半 。男方先表态 I really just try to be encouraging，再用取舍句 editorial guidance is less imp…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 He offers them ample editorial guidance. 盗用原文 editorial guidance 原词，可原文恰恰说它 less important than encouragement——他不强调指导。听到 editorial guidance 就选，正好掉进"被贬低项"的坑，且 ample（大量）更与他"只是尽量鼓励"的克制相反。 借用原文：Do they ask you to proofread their essays?
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：He recommends model essays to them. 借了 essays 这个语境词（女方确实问到 proofread their essays），但"推荐范文（model essays）"这件事男方从没说过，是凭"帮写作"语境硬造的做法。
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：proofread 这个词确实出现，但它出自女方提问 Do they ask you to proofread their essays?，是"孩子请他校对"，并非"他教孩子校对"。He teaches them proofreading. 把女方问句里的词搬来、又改成"他教校对"，既盗原词又错了施动方。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I really just try to be encouraging ↔ He gives them encouragement. be encouraging→give encouragement 形容词转名词）

questions.evidenceText: I really just try to be encouraging. I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about herself when she was a teenager?

options.text: She realized the power of reading.
Her reading opened her eyes to the world.
She began to perceive the world differently.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P9）：I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence. I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager.信号：mine + when I was a teenager 锁定她谈自己 。女方说 I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager，mine 回指 tastes…

optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：She realized the power of reading. 里的 power 出自男方 they give you the power to begin to perceive the world，是男方谈读书的话，不是女方说自己；且女方从没说她"意识到读书的力量"。既错主语又属未提及。 借用原文：open their eyes to the world
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：Her reading opened her eyes to the world. 盗用男方 read subject matter that'll open their eyes to the world 的原词 open eyes to the world，但这是男方对"孩子该读什么"的看法，主语既不是"她"、内容也非她自述。听到 open eyes 就选会被男方的话误导。 借用原文：perceive the world through the lives of others
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：She began to perceive the world differently. 盗用男方 to perceive the world through the lives of others 的 perceive the world，但这同样是男方对读书意义的论述，非女方谈自己。与 C 是一对孪生干扰，靠"主语是谁"才能切开。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（children's tastes in books change ↔ Her tastes in books changed. mine did 还原为 her tastes changed）

questions.evidenceText: I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence. I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager.

transcript.text: M: In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur. Molly, tell us about your business.
transcript.zh: M：在本期《金钱访谈》中，我们的嘉宾是莫莉·桑德斯，一名大学生，也是一位成功的年轻企业家。莫莉，给我们介绍一下你的生意吧。

transcript.text: W: Well, I sell specialty clothes through a website, mainly for women who have trouble finding suitable clothes in main street shops because of their height or weight. But I do some men's clothes too.
transcript.zh: W：嗯，我通过一个网站销售特色服装，主要面向那些因为身高或体重而难以在商业街服装店找到合适衣服的女性。不过，我也做一些男装。

transcript.text: M: How did you get started in this business at such a young age? Are you studying fashion design?
transcript.zh: M：你这么年轻，是怎么开始做这门生意的？你在学习服装设计吗？

transcript.text: W: Actually, I'm majoring in finance, but I've always loved clothes. And I started making my own at 14.
transcript.zh: W：其实，我的专业是金融，但我一直很喜欢服装。而且我从14岁起就开始自己做衣服了。

transcript.text: M: Did you have any sort of training in design or sewing? Or was it a natural ability?
transcript.zh: M：你接受过设计或缝纫方面的培训吗？还是说这是你的天赋？

transcript.text: W: I'd have to say no to both. No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters.
transcript.zh: W：这两方面都不是。没人教过我做衣服，而且我刚开始做的大多数衣服都糟糕透了。

transcript.text: M: Why did you persevere? I think most people would give up if they kept failing, especially at that age.
transcript.zh: M：你为什么坚持下来了？我想大多数人如果一直失败，都会放弃，尤其是在那个年纪。

transcript.text: W: I kept on out of necessity. As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops. So I kept trying and developed my skills over time.
transcript.zh: W：我是出于需要才坚持下来的。你也看得出来，我个子很高，在普通商店里找不到合身的衣服。所以我不断尝试，随着时间的推移逐渐提高了自己的技能。

transcript.text: M: Well, my notes say you earned $50,000 in profits last year, an extraordinary amount for a 20-year-old student. How did that happen? Did you see a gap in the market and decide to fill it?
transcript.zh: M：嗯，我的资料上说，你去年赚了5万美元的利润。对于一名20岁的学生来说，这是一笔惊人的数目。这是怎么做到的？你发现了市场空缺，然后决定填补它吗？

transcript.text: W: No. When I started university, some classmates complimented my clothes. And when I said I made them myself, other tall women started asking if I would make theirs. And I did. And before I knew it, I was an entrepreneur.
transcript.zh: W：不是。我上大学时，一些同学夸我的衣服好看。当我说衣服是我自己做的之后，其他高个子女性开始问我能不能帮她们做衣服。我答应了。没过多久，我就成了一名企业家。

transcript.text: M: So what are your plans for the future? Do you intend to open a physical store?
transcript.zh: M：那么，你对未来有什么计划？你打算开一家实体店吗？

transcript.text: W: No. I'll keep things online to keep costs down. But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants. And I hope to add to my range of designs for men.
transcript.zh: W：不打算。我会继续在线经营，以降低成本。不过，我会增加更多儿童服装，包括女孩和男孩的服装，甚至可能还会做婴儿服装。我也希望增加男装的设计种类。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman?

options.text: She is a main street store owner.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur.信号：主持人开场介绍嘉宾的同位语 。答案信号是开场白里介绍嘉宾身份的同位语 a university student and a successful young entrepreneur——访谈类听力里，嘉宾身份几乎都在…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音确实说她是 a university student，She is a university graduate. 借此设套；但一来题问我们了解到什么，主持人重点捧的是 successful entrepreneur，二来 student（在读）不等于 graduate（已毕业），身份还被偷改了。 借用原文：I sell specialty clothes through a website
optionAnalysis.A: 过度推断：后文她说 I sell specialty clothes through a website，但用网站卖衣服不等于她是做网站的设计师，She is a website designer. 是从 website 一词过度联想出来的。 借用原文：I'll keep things online to keep costs down
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：她明确说将来 I'll keep things online to keep costs down，根本不开实体店，She is a main street store owner. 与原文相反；main street 还是她顾客买不到衣服的地方，并非她开店之处。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a successful young entrepreneur ↔ She is a successful entrepreneur. 近乎同词，只省去 young）

questions.evidenceText: In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the clothes she made at first?

options.text: They were repeatedly rejected by shops.
They were popular with her classmates.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters.信号：被问者直接应答里的自我评价词 。主持人问她是否有天赋，她应答中的 most of the things I made at first were disasters 是直接评价句，disasters 这个强贬义词就是…

optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：主持人问 Or was it a natural ability?，They showed her natural talent. 盗用了 natural 一词；但她明确回答 I'd have to say no to both（天赋、培训都没有），所以显出天赋恰与原文相反。 借用原文：some classmates complimented my clothes
optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：They were repeatedly rejected by shops. 听着像创业故事，但录音从没说她最初的衣服被商店反复拒收；她说的是顾客在 main street shops 买不到合身的，张冠李戴了。
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：同学称赞她衣服确有其事——some classmates complimented my clothes，They were popular with her classmates. 借此设套；但那是她上大学后的事，不是最初（14岁）做的，时间错位。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（were disasters ↔ They were mostly failures. disasters 约等于 failures 的同义替换）

questions.evidenceText: No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters.

questions.stem: Why did the woman persevere in making clothes for herself?

options.text: She had a strong interest in doing it.
She did not like ready-made clothes.
She could not find clothes of her size.
She found clothes in shops unaffordable.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P8）：I kept on out of necessity. As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops.信号：原因短语 out of necessity 引出理由 。答案信号是因果短语 out of necessity（出于必需），其后紧跟的 I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes…

optionAnalysis.A: 答非所问：她确说过 I've always loved clothes，She had a strong interest in doing it. 借喜爱设套；但那解释的是她为何开始做衣服，题问的是为何坚持，她坚持的理由是无奈，不是兴趣。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：She found clothes in shops unaffordable. 与C都涉及商店的衣服，迷惑性强；但录音说的是找不到合身的，从未提到买不起、太贵，价格问题纯属杜撰。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：She did not like ready-made clothes. 听着合理，但录音只说商店里没有合她身的，从没说她不喜欢现成衣服；她做衣服是因买不到，不是因厌恶成衣。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops ↔ She could not find clothes of her size. fit me 约等于 of her size 的同义改写）

questions.evidenceText: I kept on out of necessity. As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops.

questions.stem: What does the woman plan to do in the future?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P12）：But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants. And I hope to add to my range of designs for men.信号：将来意图信号 I will 与 I hope to 。答案信号是 I will add more clothes for children 与 I hope to add to my range of designs…

optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：她确说 add to my range of designs for men，Add designs for women. 却把对象由 men（男士）偷换成 women（女士），方向都改错了，且她加的远不止男装。 借用原文：Are you studying fashion design?
optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：前文主持人问 Are you studying fashion design?，Study fashion design at college. 盗用了 fashion design；但她回答 I'm majoring in finance，学的是金融，更没把学时装设计当未来计划。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：Improve her marketing strategy. 听着像生意人会做的事，但录音谈未来时只说加品类、保持线上控成本，从没提改进营销策略。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（add more clothes for children ↔ Expand her business. 具体加品类等于概括的扩展生意）

transcript.text: 1 Researchers have identified a potent new antibiotic compound using artificial intelligence.
The antibiotic can kill very dangerous bacteria.

According to a study published in the journal Cell, the compound successfully removed deadly strains of bacteria in mice which are resistant to all known antibiotics. 2 The researchers say this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule.
Why does this matter?
The answer is antibiotic resistance.
This happens when bacteria develop the ability to survive the medications designed to kill them.
Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health and the problem is growing.
This makes finding new antibiotics very important.
However, in recent decades, very few have been developed, and those that have tend to be very similar to drugs already available.
The searches also tend to only focus on a narrow spectrum of chemical compounds, but this is where artificial intelligence comes in.
To find new drugs, scientists screen molecules to predict how effective they might be.
Typically, such screening is done by humans in the lab, which is both costly and slow.
Artificial intelligence is different.
It's fast, and it can process a high volume.
It can screen hundreds of millions of compounds to identify a few interesting candidates that require experimental testing.
Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic.
Some experts assert that this work signifies a paradigm shift in antibiotic discovery.
It could change drug discovery more generally.

questions.stem: What have researchers done for the first time in history?

options.text: Utilizing artificial intelligence to find a powerful new antibiotic.
Discovering bacteria which are resistant to all known antibiotics.
Identifying bacterial strains that are most harmful to human health.
Removing a deadly strain of bacteria in humans with a new antibiotic.

transcript.text: A recent study overturned what we think we know about lying. Most of us have a theory about how to tell if someone is telling a lie. We may develop that theory from observations of those people we know well and see regularly, but we tend to generalize what we gather from that unscientific daily research and make it a universal theory.
transcript.zh: 一项最新研究推翻了我们对说谎的固有认识。我们大多数人都有一套判断某人是否在说谎的理论。这套理论可能源于我们对熟悉且经常见面的人的观察，但我们往往会把从这种不科学的日常观察中得出的结论加以概括，并将其视为普遍适用的理论。

transcript.text: So we might imagine that liars have evasive eyes, or the opposite—they simply stare at you. Or perhaps it is more generally nervous behavior we associate with lies. Whatever the particular theory, it's usually based on close observation of people we know. And we get lots of practice. On average, we're lied to some 200 times per day. These are mostly harmless lies, but lies nonetheless.
transcript.zh: 因此，我们可能会认为说谎者目光闪躲，或者恰恰相反，他们只是盯着你看。又或者，我们通常会把某种更普遍的紧张行为与谎言联系起来。无论具体是哪一种理论，它通常都建立在对我们熟悉的人的细致观察之上。而且，我们有大量的实践机会。平均而言，我们每天大约会被欺骗200次。这些大多是无害的谎言，但归根结底仍然是谎言。

transcript.text: But there's a problem with our theories, even though they're based on all these observations. The average person—you and me—tested rigorously on how well we detect lies fails to do better than chance. That's well established over many studies and lots of attempts by researchers to work out reliable ways to detect lies. It's even relatively easy to fool lie detectors, the gold standard of lie detection, by training yourself in breathing techniques and symptom suppression.
transcript.zh: 然而，尽管我们的理论建立在所有这些观察之上，它们仍然存在一个问题。普通人，也就是你我，在接受严格测试以评估识别谎言的能力时，表现并不比凭猜测好。这一点已经被众多研究以及研究人员为找出可靠的测谎方法所进行的大量尝试充分证实。即使是测谎的金标准测谎仪，也相对容易被欺骗，只要通过训练掌握呼吸技巧并抑制相关生理反应即可。

transcript.text: Is there any way to get better at detecting lies? The new research offers some surprising advice. Stop looking and listen instead. It turns out that if we're unable to see the face, but rather focus on the voice of the person in question, our accuracy rate improves considerably.
transcript.zh: 有没有办法提高识别谎言的能力？这项新研究给出了令人意外的建议：不要再看，而是改为倾听。事实证明，如果我们看不到对方的脸，而是专注于相关人士的声音，我们的准确率会显著提高。

questions.stem: According to the passage, how do most people detect lying?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：We may develop that theory from observations of those people we know well and see regularly, but we tend to generalize what we gather from that unscientific daily research and make it a universal theory.信号：起源信号 develop … from 。develop that theory from observations 里的 develop … from 点明"这套判断说谎的理论来自哪里"，正是"靠什么方式"的答案落…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音反复出现 theory、universal theory，A 项 By theorization.（靠理论化）就是拿这个原词来骗；但录音说理论是"从观察中得来"，获取方式是观察，不是"靠理论化"去判断说谎。 借用原文：we tend to generalize what we gather
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音确实说了 we tend to generalize，B 项 By generalization. 就盗这个词；但 generalize 是"把观察所得再归纳推广"的后续动作，不是"多数人最初靠什么发现说谎"——题问的是 detect 的方式，那是观察。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：By conversation.（靠交谈）与 observation 词形相近，最易听混，但录音通篇没说人们靠"交谈"来识谎，属未提及。

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：They are easy to detect. 与录音相反：后文 fails to do better than chance 说人识谎并不强、谎言并不"易察觉"，此项反了。 借用原文：there's a problem with our theories
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：They are well intended.（出于善意）听上去顺理成章，但录音只说谎言"无害"，从没说它们"出于善意"，是未提及。
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：录音说人们的识谎"理论"有问题（there's a problem with our theories），They are groundless. 像是把"无根据"安到了 lies 头上；但题问的是 most lies，谎言本身并未被说成"无根据"，属张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（mostly harmless lies ↔ They are harmless. 原词 harmless 几乎直给）

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The average person—you and me—tested rigorously on how well we detect lies fails to do better than chance.信号：结论信号 fails to do better than chance 。fails to do better than chance 是这段的研究结论落点：普通人识谎"不比瞎猜强"；下一句 That's well …

questions.stem: What advice does the new research offer regarding lie detection?

options.text: Looking the speaker in the eye.
Focusing on the speaker's facial expressions.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：The new research offers some surprising advice. Stop looking and listen instead.信号：建议+对比信号 Stop … and … instead 。Stop looking and listen instead 是直白的祈使建议句，且用 Stop looking 与 listen instead 构成"…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：Looking the speaker in the eye. 属"看"派，而录音建议恰恰是 Stop looking（别看了）；它盗用了"看"这个动作来骗，方向却与建议相反。 借用原文：training yourself in breathing techniques
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：录音的 breathing 出现在第 3 段——说骗过测谎仪靠 training yourself in breathing techniques，与"新研究的建议"无关；Measuring the speaker's breathing rate. 把这个原词搬来当建议，属张冠李戴。 借用原文：if we're unable to see the face

transcript.text: Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful and undemanding; show great pleasure when a doctor comes into your room, even if the visit is brief and useless. Don't challenge anyone with authority unless you are famous or very rich.
transcript.zh: 表现得顺从、谦卑、感恩而且毫无要求；即使医生来你的病房只是短暂逗留且毫无用处，也要表现出极大的喜悦。除非你名声显赫或非常富有，否则不要挑战任何有权威的人。

transcript.text: Those are a few strategies for dealing with today's American medical establishment. What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration. But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that. In his book, A Whole New Life, novelist Reynolds Price recalls that his doctors chose a crowded hallway as the place to tell him he might have a tumor on his spinal cord. It did not occur to the two physicians that a hallway was not the most appropriate place for that particular piece of news.
transcript.zh: 这些是应对当今美国医疗机构的几种策略。患者想要的是受到尊重和体贴的对待。但依我的经验，愿意这样做的医院和医生太少了。小说家雷诺兹·普莱斯在其著作《全新的生活》中回忆说，他的医生选择了一条拥挤的走廊作为告诉他脊髓上可能长有肿瘤的地点。两位医生都没有想到，走廊并不是传达这一特殊消息最恰当的地方。

transcript.text: My surgeon, who is in his mid-thirties, looks tired. He has been overwhelmed with patients who have fallen on the winter ice. He is a witty man, but sometimes his wit is unwelcome.
transcript.zh: 我的外科医生三十多岁，看起来很疲惫。他一直被那些在冬季结冰路面上摔倒的患者弄得应接不暇。他是个风趣的人，但有时他的幽默并不受欢迎。

transcript.text: "The health insurance company Blue Cross wants me to put you out in the snow tomorrow afternoon," he tells me after I have been in the hospital for more than a week. I'm terrified because I have no idea where to go. I cannot walk or even lift my leg a few inches. The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot. But my complaints about her only annoy my surgeon. "I have to work with these people," he tells my friend, Dr. Karen Brudney, when she mercifully intervenes on my behalf and arranges for me to be transferred to another hospital.
transcript.zh: “医疗保险公司蓝十字希望我明天下午把你赶到雪地里去，”我住院一个多星期后，他对我说。我吓坏了，因为我完全不知道该去哪里。我无法行走，甚至连腿抬高几英寸都做不到。医院的社会工作者让我觉得她是个笨蛋。但我对她的抱怨只让我的外科医生感到恼火。“我还得和这些人共事，”当我的朋友凯伦·布鲁德尼医生出面替我求情，并安排把我转到另一家医院时，他对她说道。

transcript.text: "If you say one negative thing, they get defensive," she tells me later. "They have this kind of institutional loyalty. Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse. When people know you have their names, they behave better. And," Brudney adds, "if you, as a patient, suggest that you might like to control even part of the situation or be consulted or informed, then you are considered difficult. They want you to be totally passive. The entire health care system, particularly hospitals and nursing homes, exists for reasons that have nothing to do with taking care of patients. Patients are incidental."
transcript.zh: “只要你说一句负面的话，他们就会采取防御姿态，”她后来对我说。“他们有一种机构忠诚感。一定要带一位代言人，也就是说，带另一个人和你一起去医院，并把每一个问题及其答案、每一位医生和护士的姓名全都记下来。当人们知道你记住了他们的名字时，他们的表现会好一些。而且，”布鲁德尼补充道，“如果作为患者，你表示希望对哪怕一部分情况进行掌控，或者希望被征求意见、被告知情况，那么你就会被视为难相处的人。他们希望你完全被动。整个医疗保健体系，尤其是医院和养老院的存在，都是出于与照料患者毫无关系的原因。患者只是附带的存在。”

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P2）：What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration. But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that.信号：转折 But + 程度词 too few 。答案落在转折词后：But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that。前半句说…

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：They want you to be totally passive.信号：want 表期望 + totally 强调 。答案句以 They want you to be totally passive 直白给出期望：want 正对题干 expect，totally 加重语气强调这正是医院想…

transcript.text: There are probably teams you've worked with but you never want to work with again. But there must have also been other teams that you would prize reuniting with professionally. In other words, your team had vitality. Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up.
transcript.zh: 你可能曾与一些团队共事过，但再也不想与他们合作。然而，肯定也有一些其他团队，是你非常珍视能在职业上与之重聚的。换句话说，你的团队具有活力。当人们与团队同事建立的联系使他们即使在团队解散后仍保持联系时，团队就会产生这种活力。

transcript.text: What characteristics of a team make its members more likely to stay in contact despite no longer working together? This question has been answered recently in a study published in a business journal.
transcript.zh: 团队具有什么样的特征，才能使其成员即使不再一起工作，也更有可能保持联系？最近，一项发表于商业期刊的研究回答了这个问题。

transcript.text: One of the two key factors the research team discovered is sameness. Specifically, sharing the same gender or ethnic origin. The more members of a team share similar demographics, the more inclined they will be to remain associates long after the team has served its purpose. After ties are established, similarity strengthens them. As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration. In effect, people tend to create stronger and longer-lasting connections with similar others. Someone who looks and sounds different from us may have the resources we need to be more successful. Yet, we find them to be significantly less credible simply because they are different. If you are a fierce advocate of workplace diversity, you'll no doubt be horrified by such a revelation.
transcript.zh: 研究团队发现的两个关键因素之一是相似性，具体来说，就是拥有相同的性别或族裔背景。一个团队成员的人口统计特征越相似，他们就越倾向于在团队完成使命很久之后仍保持同事关系。联系建立之后，相似性会进一步巩固这种联系。因此，他们会更加信任并相互理解这些人，这促使他们寻求进一步合作的机会。实际上，人们往往会与相似的人建立更牢固、更持久的联系。与我们外貌和声音不同的人，或许拥有帮助我们取得更大成功所需的资源。然而，仅仅因为他们与众不同，我们就会发现自己明显不那么信任他们。如果你是职场多元化的坚定倡导者，毫无疑问会对这样的发现感到震惊。

transcript.text: The second factor identified by the researchers is the quality of the relationships among the team members. The more they trust one another, share the same goals and depend on each other for the achievement of those goals, the stronger their chances of maintaining their connections, despite no longer working as one team. Teams with quality relationships have a shared belief that it's safe to take risks with each other, and their members are obliged to share the workload and help out.
transcript.zh: 研究人员确定的第二个因素是团队成员之间关系的质量。他们彼此越信任，目标越一致，并且越依赖彼此来实现这些目标，即使不再作为一个团队工作，他们维持彼此联系的可能性就越大。关系良好的团队拥有一种共同信念，即彼此合作承担风险是安全的；其成员也有义务分担工作量并互相提供帮助。

transcript.text: From personal experience, I can see both the truth and the inconsistency of such studies. The truth is some of my closest friendships were formed as a result of having worked together on teams, and I actively seek opportunities to work with them again. The inconsistency, though, is that I've never worked for a team more successful and cohesive than the one of which I am a member right now. And yet, the four of us have very little in common and are completely different demographically. So I am unlikely to question the value of a diverse workforce.
transcript.zh: 根据个人经历，我既能看出这类研究的真实性，也能看出其中的不一致之处。真实之处在于，我最亲密的一些友谊源于我们曾一起在团队中工作，而我也会主动寻找再次与他们合作的机会。然而，不一致之处在于，我从未在一个比我目前所在团队更加成功、更加团结的团队中工作过。可是，我们四个人几乎没有共同之处，在人口统计特征上也完全不同。因此，我不太可能质疑多元化劳动力的价值。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about a team with vitality?

options.text: Its members work together despite risks of failure.
It prioritizes recruiting young energetic members.
Its members stay in touch even after it breaks up.
It grows more and more mature professionally.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up.信号：下定义句 "Vitality comes about when…" 。录音用 Vitality comes about when 给"活力"正式下定义，紧跟其后的 they stay connected even a…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 的 risks of failure 借用了第 4 段 safe to take risks with each other 里的 risks 一词，但那是讲"优质关系"、不是 vitality 的定义，听到 risk 就选会偏题。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：B 说团队 prioritizes recruiting young energetic members（优先招募有活力的年轻成员），录音通篇没说招募，纯属臆造，多半是被 vitality 的"活力"联想出来的。
optionAnalysis.D: 过度推断：D 称团队 grows more and more mature professionally，录音定义 vitality 时只字未提"专业上越来越成熟"，这是顺着"好团队"想当然推出来的，原文无据。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（they stay connected even after the team breaks up ↔ Its members stay in touch even after it breaks up stay connected = stay in touch）

options.text: Their differences are likely to impact productivity.

Their connections strengthen with the passage of time.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：After ties are established, similarity strengthens them. As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration.信号：因果信号 "As a result…seek…collaboration" 。录音先说 similarity strengthens them，再用因果词 As a result 引出 motivates them …

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：A 称 differences are likely to impact productivity，但录音研究结论强调的是相似 similarity strengthens them，A 取了相反的一极（differences），且 productivity 录音根本没提，方向与原文相反。 借用原文：similarity strengthens them
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：C 说 connections strengthen with the passage of time，借了录音 similarity strengthens them 的 strengthen 一词，却把原因偷换成"随时间推移"——录音说让纽带变牢的是相似，不是时间。 借用原文：greater trust and mutual understanding
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 说 mutual understanding stems from a common goal，mutual understanding 确实出自录音 greater trust and mutual understanding，但录音说相互理解来自"相似"、不是来自"共同目标"（common goal 属第 4 段另一因素），强加了错误因果。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（similarity strengthens them ↔ Their similarity is conducive to strengthens = conducive to）

questions.evidenceText: After ties are established, similarity strengthens them. As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration.

options.text: It is connected by a unique mechanism.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：And yet, the four of us have very little in common and are completely different demographically.信号：转折 "And yet" 后才是真意 。前句说当前团队最 successful and cohesive，紧接 And yet 转折，引出 have very little in common and are com…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 说团队 goals are quite inconsistent，借了录音 the inconsistency 一词，但那个 inconsistency 指的是"研究结论与说话者经历不一致"，不是说这支团队的目标不一致，原词被挪错了对象。 借用原文：have very little in common

optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D 说团队 connected by a unique mechanism，录音从未提任何"独特机制"，是凭"这么成功一定有什么特别机制"想象出来的，原文无据。

transcript.text: An American researcher who studied 600 millionaires found how rich you can get comes down to six wealth factors. She found that six behaviors are related to net worth potential, regardless of age or income. These were thriftiness, confidence, responsibility, planning, focus and social indifference.
transcript.zh: 一位研究了6亿名百万富翁的美国研究人员发现，一个人能够变得多么富有，归根结底取决于六个财富因素。她发现，无论年龄或收入如何，六种行为都与净资产潜力有关。这些行为分别是节俭、自信、责任感、规划、专注以及不在意社会评价。

transcript.text: Being thrifty comes as no great surprise. Spending above your means, spending instead of saving for retirement, spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy, makes you a slave to the paycheck. "Even with an astronomical level of income," she wrote, "to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%."
transcript.zh: 节俭并不令人感到意外。入不敷出地消费、不为退休储蓄而消费、预想着自己会变得富有而消费，都会使你沦为薪水的奴隶。她写道：“即使收入达到天文数字，要想合理地积累财富，专家也建议将收入的20%存起来，靠剩下的80%生活。”

transcript.text: Having confidence is another key characteristic, as it helps people to be thrifty. It takes confidence to live within your means. It also takes confidence to invest properly. Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investments alone and focus on a long-term investment plan. But people can't invest or manage their own money without accepting responsibility for the outcomes. Many millionaires take on personal responsibility, and most also happen to be self-made, meaning they didn't acquire their wealth through luck. Millionaires don't count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don't blame anyone else if they fall short. They focus on things they can control and align their daily habits to the goals they have set for themselves. They tend to be goal-oriented and hard workers, which enables them to plan financially and focus on seeing those plans through. 92% of the millionaires surveyed developed a long term plan for their money and 97% almost always achieved the goals they set for themselves.
transcript.zh: 拥有自信是另一个关键特征，因为这能帮助人们保持节俭。量入为出需要自信。正确地进行投资同样需要自信。财务规划师建议，不要凭情绪做出投资决定，而应放任投资自行运作，并专注于长期投资计划。但如果不对结果承担责任，人们就无法投资或管理自己的资金。许多百万富翁都承担个人责任，而且大多数人还碰巧是白手起家，这意味着他们并非靠运气获得财富。百万富翁不会指望别人让自己变得富有，如果没有达到目标，他们也不会责怪别人。他们专注于自己能够控制的事情，并使日常习惯与自己设定的目标保持一致。他们往往以目标为导向且勤奋努力，这使他们能够进行财务规划，并专注于贯彻落实这些计划。接受调查的百万富翁中，有92%为自己的资金制定了长期计划，97%几乎总能实现自己设定的目标。

transcript.text: And it is these behaviors that make it easy for them to be socially indifferent. They resist lifestyle creep, the tendency to spend more whenever one earns more. Essentially, they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others or what they have acquired. Instead of being focused on what might make them happy today, they're focused on their long-term wealth-building plan.
transcript.zh: 正是这些行为，使他们很容易做到不在意社会评价。他们抵制生活方式膨胀，也就是一个人收入增加后便倾向于增加消费。他们基本不会屈服于购买最新产品的压力，也不会为了与他人保持一致或追赶他人已经拥有的东西而消费。他们关注的不是今天可能让自己感到快乐的事物，而是长期积累财富的计划。

options.text: Putting aside twenty percent of one's earnings.
Spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy.
Living off a small proportion of one's income.
Saving as much as one can possibly manage.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）："Even with an astronomical level of income," she wrote, "to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%."信号：原词 recommend 直接领出建议 。答案句直接出现题干同款词 experts recommend，紧跟其后的 saving 20% of your income 就是被推荐的做法——"建议/推荐"类动词后面那句…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 的 Spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy 几乎照搬原文 spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy，但原文是把它当作让人沦为"工资奴隶"的反面行为来批评，不是专家推荐的做法，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：living off the remaining 80%

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: In the long view, the human relationship with forests has been one of brutal destruction, but even it carries elements of slow hope. In the Middle Ages, there was no shortage of timber in most parts of the world, and few saw cutting down forests as a problem. Yet in 1548 the people of Venice estimated that an important timber supply would last only 30 years at their current rate of usage—but different forest management would make it possible to meet the demand for many centuries to come. The idea of preserving resources came out of a concern for the future: a fear of using up resources faster than they could be replenished(补充).

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Economic interests were at the core of this understanding of trees and forests. It would take more than three centuries before scientists began to understand that timber production is not the only, and possibly not the most important, function of forests. The late 19th and early 20th century saw an increasing recognition that forests serve as habitats for countless animal and plant species that all rely on each other. They take over protective functions against soil erosion and landslides(塌方); they make a significant contribution to the water balance as they prevent surface runoff; they filter dirt particles, greenhouse gases and radioactive substances from the air; they produce oxygen; they provide spaces for recreation and they preserve historic and prehistoric remains. As a result, forests around the world have been set aside as parks or wilderness areas.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Recent years have seen a big change in our view of forests. Peter Wohlleben's book The Hidden Life of Trees (2015), an international bestseller, suggests that trees can warn each other of danger through a "wood wide web" of roots and fungi(真菌). They support each other through sharing of nutrients and information, and they even keep ancient stumps alive by feeding them solutions of sugars. Such insights have made us aware of deep ecological relationships between humans and the more-than-human world.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Awareness of ecologies is a recent phenomenon. It was not until the 1940s that the concept of the "environment" embracing all living and nonliving things developed. In the 1970s, the term "environment" gained currency, becoming widely adopted in the English and Romance languages, and as "Umwelt" ("surrounding world") in German. The emergence of the idea led to the rise of environmental agencies, regulations and environmental studies, and to environmental science as new, integrated academic disciplines. It was in 1956 that the very first bachelor of science in environmental studies was awarded, at the State University of New York College of Forestry at Syracuse. Since the 1970s—with the rise of "environmentalism"—environmental studies programmes have sprung up at hundreds of universities. There is (slow) hope in the fact that scholars from many different disciplines have adopted the term "environment" over the past decades. They are exploring intricate connections within and between complex ecologies, as well as the impact that human environment-making (through techno-industrial, economic and other manipulative developments) has had on the biosphere.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The rise of the idea of the environment and a scholarly understanding of ecological processes has influenced new technologies and also politics. We have come to ask questions about vulnerability and risk, world ecologies, and the relationship between nature and power. The search for an adequate response to climate change occupies centre stage in international diplomacy.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Social and environmental activists, scientists and indigenous groups have called the Paris Agreement of the United Nations Climate Change Conference in December 2015 insufficient, weak, or compromised. To some extent, they are right: climate change has already destroyed tens of thousands of livelihoods, and the situation will worsen in the near future for millions of mostly poorer people, who will join the ranks of those who have already been displaced by climate change and extreme weather events. But the Paris Conference nevertheless marked a historic step toward the recognition of the need for action on climate change, the cutting of carbon emissions, and world cooperation. There were 195 nations that came to the table in Paris and agreed to limits on emissions. Historically, nothing comparable had happened prior to this. Before the 20th century, a handful of scientists had been interested in the theoretical relationship between greenhouse gases and climate change, but only the empirical evidence accumulated since the late 20th century established a clear connection between the burning of fossil fuels and a vastly accelerated rise in global temperatures.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The current crisis is not the first that humans have encountered, and a look at the struggles with pollution in recent history reveals transformations that once seemed unimaginable. The "London fog" that came to define the capital through British novels and thrillers is in reality smog or smoke, a legacy of industrialisation. After a century of ignorance, London was hit by the Great Smog of December 1952—the worst air-pollution event in the history of the United Kingdom which caused the deaths of approximately 12,000 people. Shortly thereafter, public initiatives and political campaigns led to strict regulations and new laws, including the Clean Air Act (1956). Today, London has effectively reduced traffic emissions through the introduction of a Congestion Charge Zone in 2003, and an Ultra Low Emission Zone in 2019.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Scientific evidence that we are living in an era of climate change, resource exhaustion and potential ecological disaster is overwhelming. How do we motivate a public exhausted by never-ending scenarios of doom and disaster, when the challenges seem so huge and so impossible to solve? Statistics about extinction and the gloom of decline will not in themselves get us out of our often self-created ecological traps: instead, they are more likely to result in paralysis and inaction.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: We need stories and histories of change and transformation: ecological stories that make us confront the fact that human power is potentially destructive, and that the survival of our species on this planet depends on the preservation of soil and water, and the habitats and ecological systems.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: It is time that we showed successes and accelerations in ecological awareness, action and restoration: stories that include past successes and future visions about the rise of urban gardening and of renaturalised riverscapes, of successful protests against polluted air and water, of the rise of regional markets and slow food, and the planting of trees around the globe, of initiatives and enterprises that work towards ecological restoration. The reality of ecological curses seems far greater than the power of the hopes left at the bottom of Pandora's box. But if we believe that nothing can be changed, then we are giving up our opportunity to act.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Today's saving powers will not come from a deus ex machina(解围之神). In an ever-more complex and synthetic world, our saving powers won't come from a single source, and certainly not from a too-big-to-fail approach or from those who have been drawn into the whirlpool of our age of speed. Hope can work as a wakeup call. It acknowledges setbacks. The concept of slow hope suggests that we can't expect things to change overnight. If the ever-faster exhaustion of natural resources (in ecological terms) and the "shrinking of the present" (in social terms) are urgent problems of humans, then cutting down on exhaustive practices and working towards a "stretching of the present" will be ways to move forward.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Since American idol star Taryn Southern started composing music with AI in 2017, musicians all over the world have begun wondering about the implications of AI and modern technology where music production is concerned. Using AI in the creation of music is perceived by some as a helpful tool and by others as almost "the beginning of the end".

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: In Taryn's case, AI software enabled her to communicate melodies and chords that she didn't know how to put together herself. The end product was therefore a collaborative effort, rather than a piece entirely produced by technology. Taryn's story has a distinctly positive feel that highlights the advantages of using AI in music production. It can serve as a source of inspiration, and as an ideal jumping-off point should a musician be hit with writer's block(文思枯竭).

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Contrary to seeing AI as a tool, some musicians consider it to be hugely detrimental to the music scene. At the moment, because such technology is still so young, the music it's producing is not necessarily what we want to hear. In short, it's not of great quality. Those who have produced their own music, or even fans of authentic, artistic music, will also argue that a computer could never emulate the work (and human touch) of a true musician.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Music has been an integral part of the story of humans for ages; in fact, the first known piece of music is believed to be around 3,400 years old. Songs have long been used as a means of communicating messages and folk stories, covering everything from societal ethics to world history. Since many people see music as such an inherently human expression, it is often considered as too precious to impart to technology. The thought of a computer generating a "random" piece of music that hasn't been painstakingly created by an artist is almost seen as sacrilegious(亵渎神圣的).

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Regardless of which side of the argument you fall on, it seems likely that the use of AI in music production will only become more frequent. Our modern world is preoccupied with technological advancements. Instead of shying away from the idea of this bleak future, the best approach to take is one of optimism and curiosity. While there are always bound to be stubborn old-school musicians who refuse to use tech, music producers should consider AI as something to be embraced. AI music software is still very much in its infancy, but with more investors interested in the development and outcomes of such technology, and considering the rapid growth rate of other tech advances in recent years, it's only a matter of time before AI-produced music is seen as the new norm.
